checkpoint_review: The Router's checkpoint verdicts are largely accurate and well-reasoned. The classification of the 'ostiole' checkpoint as untestable is correct due to occlusion. The Router correctly identified the presence of key fig features (shape, skin texture, internal pulp/seeds). However, the Router was slightly lenient regarding the 'pale slices' on the right; while it noted them as a texture anomaly, it did not flag them as a potential semantic hallucination (e.g., onion/garlic) which is a significant deviation from the 'fig' class label if they are indeed foreign objects.
artifact_review: The Router identified a 'texture_anomaly' (severity 2) for the pale slices and 'blur' (severity 1). The Topology Boundary Auditor found high confidence (0.9361) for the mask of these slices, suggesting they are coherent objects, but this does not confirm their biological identity as fig parts. The Perceptual Quality Auditor found no graphics-level distortions. I agree with the severity ratings but elevate the concern about the pale slices: if they are onions, this is a semantic artifact (hallucination), not just a texture issue. The blur is acceptable depth-of-field. No new structural artifacts (melting/fusion) were found by experts or myself.
alignment_reasoning: The image strongly aligns with the 'fig' class. Both fine-grained classifiers confidently identified the whole fruit and the halved interior as 'fig' (logit score 7.89 vs ~2.3 for next best). All testable checkpoints passed. The only alignment ambiguity is the identity of the pale slices, but since the primary subjects (the figs) are perfectly aligned, the score remains high.
artifact_reasoning: The primary artifact is the ambiguous nature of the pale slices on the right. While structurally coherent (high mask confidence), their visual appearance resembles onion layers more than fig skin or flesh, suggesting a minor semantic hallucination or generation ambiguity. This prevents a perfect artifact score. The rest of the image is clean, with natural lighting and no structural melting or fusion.
key_defects: Ambiguous pale slices on the right resembling onion/garlic rather than fig parts (semantic ambiguity/hallucination risk)
Slight softness at the boundary of the halved fig and bowl (minor generation smoothing)
